key_insight: A hybrid deterministic and LLM-agent translator converts quantum MLIR dialects to QIR, using dual-backend testing to check behavioral agreement.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce custom compiler work when moving quantum workflows between frameworks and runtimes, though materials-science applications were not evaluated.
method: Use deterministic translation for known Catalyst and Quake dialects.
Route unseen dialects to an LLM agent and failed deterministic outputs to repair.
Compare independent simulator outputs using total variation distance; use inline context and a guardrail assembler for smaller models.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 circuit-dialect pairs with average TVD similarity above 95%; four of six models generated valid logical-level QIR for unseen FTQC on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR does not alone establish semantic equivalence, and unseen-dialect generalization remains supported by limited evaluation.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
